name: Jaalah
overview: Jaalah is a male figure identified in Scripture as a servant of Solomon, as noted in Ezra 2:55. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details, making his primary biblical significance his service under Solomon. The limited information confines his profile to his role within the royal household.
namesAndTitles: The individual is known by the names Jaalah and Jaala, as recorded in Ezra 2:56 and Nehemiah 7:58 respectively. Neither name is given with a specific meaning or divine origin in the text, so they are simply proper names without additional semantic insight.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Jaalah beyond his designation as Solomon's servant. No other relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jaalah's significance lies in his association with Solomon, one of Israel's most notable kings, indicating a trusted position within the royal service. His mention in the post-exilic genealogical records in Ezra and Nehemiah highlights the continuity of those connected to Solomon's reign. While not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion reflects the preservation of servant names linked to the Davidic monarchy.
